text.p: The National Hockey League, less than a week into its season, levied its second and third suspensions Tuesday, hitting Rangers star centre Mark Messier and Oilers winger Louie DeBrusk for separate incidents.
Messier was suspended two games without pay and fined the maximum $1,000 for slamming Florida Panthers left wing Mike Hough from behind on Sunday.

DeBrusk was suspended for at least one game for a slashing incident Sunday against Vancouver Canucks defenceman Dana Murzyn. The league reserves the right to extend the suspension pending further review.
Messier slammed Hough into the boards from behind and was given a major penalty and a game misconduct.

"The fact that no major injury resulted on the play is fortuitous but does not excuse the dangerous type of hit by Mr Messier against his opponent," NHL senior vice president and director of hockey operations Brian Burke said.
"Mr Hough was unable to protect himself. We view any hit from behind as a very serious and dangerous act and this decision reflects that view."
Messier will miss Tuesday night's rematch in Florida and Thursday's game with the Dallas Stars.

DeBrusk, 25, will not play in Tuesday's game at Toronto, pending a hearing Wednesday. DeBrusk, who has played parts of five seasons in the NHL, is known as an enforcer. He has just 17 goals and 723 penalty minutes in his career.
New Jersey Devils defenceman Scott Stevens earned the dubious distinction of drawing the first suspension of the season.
